In the toy sleeve

The tiger kit

Four punch-out cardboard pieces, no glue, no scissors. On the back of the sheet: where tigers live, what they eat, and one small thing a kid can do for them this week.

Every animal's base slots into the others. Twelve kits make one forest.

  • Four ingredients, no fine print. If it isn't on the front, it isn't in the chocolate.
  • Honest about sugar. We sweeten with jaggery and we still call it sugar. We use less, and we print the grams where you can see them.
  • Cardboard, not plastic. The kit is printed board that goes in the recycling when the forest gets too big. Nothing ends up in a drawer of broken plastic.
  • Toy and treat kept apart. The kit travels in its own sealed sleeve behind the bar, with big pieces made for ages three and up and certified to India's toy safety standard.

From tree to treat

Grown under coconut palms.

In the Godavari delta, cacao grows in the shade of coconut palms, next to the paddy fields. Drag along the river to follow one bean all the way to a brick.

  1. 01

    Shade

    Cacao trees grow under coconut palms. Farmers get a second harvest from the same land.

  2. 02

    Pods

    Ripe pods are cut by hand. Inside: sweet white pulp and about forty beans.

  3. 03

    Ferment

    Beans rest in wooden boxes under banana leaves for about six days. This is where the flavour is born.

  4. 04

    Sun-dry

    A week on raised beds under the delta sun, turned by hand until they rattle.

  5. 05

    Roast & grind

    Slow roast, crack, winnow, then stone-grind for days until it's silk.

  6. 06

    Bar

    Tempered, poured into small bars and wrapped in foil, next to a sealed cardboard kit.

  7. 07

    Small hands

    The tiger gets built on the kitchen table. The bar gets shared. The forest grows by one animal.

For parents

The questions you'd ask in the aisle.

How is this better than a chocolate with a plastic toy?

The chocolate is real single-origin chocolate with four ingredients. The toy is a cardboard animal kids actually build, and it connects to every other Vana animal, so it keeps getting played with instead of ending up in a drawer.

Is it sugar-free?

No, and we won't pretend. Jaggery is sugar. We keep it low, size the pack for one sitting, and print the sugar grams on the front so you can decide in two seconds.

What about allergies?

The kids' bricks contain milk. We are building them nut-free from day one so they can go into school tiffins and birthday bags.

Is the toy safe for small kids?

The kit is sealed in its own sleeve, away from the chocolate. Pieces are large and made for ages three and up, and every kit is tested to India's toy safety standard before it goes on sale.

Will it melt in Indian summers?

Every bar travels in a foil inner, and in summer we ship in insulated cartons. Like any real chocolate, it's happiest somewhere cool.

Why "Vana"?

Vana means forest. Every brick starts in one, and every pack is an animal that lives in one.
